claims.claim_text: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically identifies hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims within essays.
claims.evidence_span: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically detects hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays.

claims.claim_text: The citation checker identifies fabricated references instantly to help educators maintain academic integrity.
claims.evidence_span: Our citation checker identifies these hallucinated references instantly, helping educators maintain academic integrity without spending time on manual verification.

claims.claim_text: Advanced citation verification technology highlights specific sentences likely to contain incorrect or hallucinated citations.
claims.evidence_span: Get in-depth analysis highlighting specific sentences likely to contain hallucinated or incorrect citations, allowing educators to focus verification efforts on the most suspicious citations and claims rather than reviewing every source.

claims.claim_text: An artificial intelligence hallucination is a response generated by AI containing false or misleading information presented as fact.
claims.evidence_span: In the field of artificial intelligence (AI), a hallucination or artificial hallucination (also called bullshitting, confabulation, delusion, or mirage) is a response generated by AI that contains false or misleading information presented as fact.

claims.claim_text: Symbolic artificial intelligence models generally do not produce hallucinations, unlike large language models.
claims.evidence_span: Symbolic artificial intelligence models generally do not produce hallucinations, unlike large language models.

claims.claim_text: The Cambridge dictionary updated its definition of hallucination in 2023 to include the AI-specific sense.
claims.evidence_span: In 2023, the Cambridge dictionary updated its definition of hallucination to include this new sense specific to the field of AI.

claims.claim_text: AI hallucinations refer to statements made by the system that are factually incorrect, illogical, or not substantiated by credible sources.
claims.evidence_span: AI hallucinations refer to statements made by the system which are either factually incorrect, illogical, or not substantiated by any credible sources but sound coherent and fluent on the face of it.

claims.claim_text: The survey reviews major detection and verification paradigms, including retrieval-augmented generation and automated fact-checking.
claims.evidence_span: Subsequently, we examine major detection and verification paradigms, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), factuality evaluation metrics, automated fact-checking, natural language inference (NLI), knowledge-grounded reasoning, multi-model verification, and self-reflection-based approaches.

claims.claim_text: AI hallucinations are instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant or entirely fabricated.
claims.evidence_span: AI hallucinations are instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant or entirely fabricated.

claims.claim_text: Core factual hallucinations occur when an AI tool states information that is objectively false about the world.
claims.evidence_span: Factual hallucinations occur when an AI tool states information that is objectively false about the world.

claims.claim_text: Contextual hallucinations happen when the AI relies on general training data instead of specific contextual data supplied in a prompt.
claims.evidence_span: Contextual hallucinations happen when the AI is supposed to answer a prompt by using specific contextual data, such as a document or database, but instead relies on its general training data.

claims.claim_text: An artificial intelligence hallucination is when a language model produces content that sounds authoritative and well-reasoned but is factually wrong or entirely made up.
claims.evidence_span: An AI hallucination is when a language model produces content that sounds authoritative and well-reasoned but is factually wrong or entirely made up.

claims.claim_text: Large language models generate text by predicting upcoming words based on patterns in training data rather than consulting authoritative sources.
claims.evidence_span: They generate text by predicting what words should come next based on patterns in training data, not by consulting authoritative sources or verifying facts.

claims.claim_text: Stanford research found that specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time.
claims.evidence_span: Stanford research found that even specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time.
